newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips mixed, SAX index down 0.31 pts.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips mixed, SAX index down 0.31 pts.

text.p: 1500 GMT - Slovak blue chips close mixed in heavier trading on Bratislava Stock Exchange on Thursday, with losses to the average price of Nafta shares dragging the share index down.
* VSZ down 10 at 620, Slovnaft down four at 931, VUB up five at 1,835, Nafta up 49 at 2,050.
* Overall volume 543,424 shares, turnover 549.51 million crowns.
Slovak blue chips closed mixed on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, with losses to the average price of Nafta shares dragging the SAX index down 0.31 points to 208.34.
Nafta closed up 49 at 2,050, but its average price -- used for calculating the index -- eased by 1.51 percent, accounting for the largest part of the index's fall.

"Nafta's real price is around 2,000 crowns, and it seems that somebody was deliberately holding it higher, maybe with expectations of something at the upcoming extraordinary shareholders' meeting," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings.
Nafta has called an extraordinary shareholders meeting for September 26, following the state's controversial privatisation of 45.9 percent stake to an as-yet undisclosed company.
Slovak's largest commercial bank VUB closed up five crowns at 1,835, with brokers considering the price as real and comfortable for trading.
"But investors who bought the share during the period of artificially higher price above 2,000 crowns are now reluctant to sell their holdings," Sykora said.
Oil refiner Slovnaft closed down four at 931, but brokers said the correction did not indicate any significant changes.

Steel producer VSZ lost 10 crowns to close at 620. Brokers said there was not stronger demand for the share, as offers to sell would be at around 650 to 660 crowns, which the investor appeared unwilling to accept.

Overall volume increased to 543,424 shares on Thursday, from 111,520 shares traded on Wednesday, turnover rose to 549.51 million, from 98.32 million on Wednesday. -- Peter Laca, Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-210-3687
